summary: The change replaces whole-record fallback slots in src/repair/loop-live-inputs.ts with a per-read semaphore of eight (2 * LIVE_INPUT_READ_CONCURRENCY), so a finished issue read releases capacity for another record's PR/check chain while the eight-read peak is preserved. Slot accounting hands off to the next waiter without re-incrementing and always decrements or hands off in finally, so no slot leaks on throws, synchronous port errors, or the run-deadline rejection. The new deadline gate inside readFallback is reached only through fallback callers that already catch or use Promise.allSettled, and primeFallback still primes repositories serially with no batch/fallback overlap, so peak reads and once-per-record reads are unchanged. New fake-port tests cover the eight-request peak and elapsed bound for 60 records, the queued-read deadline boundary, and unchanged-input skips, and neither the watchdog thresholds nor any review, CI or accounting gate is touched.

evidence: src/repair/loop-live-inputs.ts now bounds fallback reads individually at FALLBACK_READ_CONCURRENCY (8) with a slot handoff that survives throws, so PR/check chains of different records pipeline instead of occupying whole-record slots; this targets the identified cause of a failed batch falling back to per-record reads.

tests/repair/loop-live-inputs-fallback_test.ts adds fake-port regressions: 60 records finish within 24s with peak 8 concurrent reads and 181 calls, and queued reads do not start after the run deadline.
No threshold change: src/host/throughput-watchdog-thresholds.ts is absent from the changed-path manifest, so no limit was raised to make the metric pass.
Review, CI, P0 and accounting gates are untouched: the manifest lists only src/repair/loop-live-inputs.ts and its two fake-port test files.
